name: తెలుగు
description: Telugu from the script upward. The alphabet is not a preliminary here but the first third of the course: an abugida of fifty-two letters, each consonant carrying a vowel of its own, is a system to be understood rather than a list to be memorised — and it is drilled at length before a single sentence is asked for.
attribution: Letter inventory and classification follow the traditional వర్ణమాల as taught in Telugu schools; transliteration is ISO 15919. Grammar written after the manner of Ivy Kellerman Reed, A Complete Grammar of Esperanto (1910).
